experiences.text: Skip advising tests to avoid private helpers like render._ack_skill_ref in favor of the public render path — test-access style refactoring suggestions are dismissed here.

Lead with the concrete silent-failure bugs in the enforcement path — ENFORCE=true with empty/unset TOUCHSTONE_TAXONOMY_TYPES becomes a no-op, a single-type whitelist zero-advantages every group into 0 candidates, and cache paths outside rollout (introspection/merge) that don't fold allowed_types into their keys silently bypass the whitelist — because these directly reopen the reward-misalignment root cause this PR claims to fix.

Demand auditable evidence — pip-audit artifacts, run links, reproducible commands — for supply-chain claims like 'zero known vulnerabilities', and check the audit is a fail-closed CI gate rather than a one-off manual run.
Do not speculate about hardcoded threshold values needing configurability or significance testing unless the repo already uses such patterns.
Avoid deep hypothetical false-positive analysis on regex patterns without evidence of actual false positives in real data.
Do not demand audit output or CI artifacts be attached in-diff to back supply-chain claims; evidence requests scoped outside a changelog-only PR get dismissed.
Close the remaining dual-source risk: the inline 时序要点 must stay in sync with SKILL.md §4, so add a keyword-parity guard test or explicitly record the accepted drift risk in the docstring.

Reserve PRA-POSSIBLE_ISSUE for genuine correctness risks in the change itself — like the type-level kind:suppress seed on seeds.yaml silently discarding real bugs despite the stated subset-only intent, or the 裸 try/except vs 裸 except terminology collision breaking detection — and never spend it on process chores like renumbering greps or regenerated-file drift, which is exactly how the lower-reward reviews diluted it.

Reserve PRA-REVIEW for the recommendations reviewers independently converge on — derive the effective taxonomy in code as labels ∪ {PRA-REVIEW} instead of hand-editing vars.TOUCHSTONE_TAXONOMY_TYPES, and add a per-unknown-type drop counter at merge_candidates so vocabulary drift is observable rather than silently zeroing rewards.

Do not spend a note on MAINTAINABILITY for hand-edited data JSON; the script-commit and auditability ask is already delivered under TESTABILITY, and the maintainability framing drew the lowest reward.
Refrain from auditing implementation-level security measures based solely on documentation text.
Prioritize verifying the exact semantic behavior of edge cases like the '0' value to ensure it disables the limit as intended.
Confirm that the downstream consumer code correctly parses the new variable states defined in the workflow configuration.
Do not flag mixed language comments unless the repository has a strict English-only policy.
Do not request documentation updates for internal CI variable wiring changes.
Do not request removal of historical context from inline comments that explain the rationale for the change.
Propose the cheap guardrail reviewers accept on release PRs: a small CI/unit check that touchstone.__version__ equals the newest CHANGELOG [x.y.z] heading.
Highlight concrete logic discrepancies, such as function signature mismatches between test suites and their corresponding implementations.
Ignore warnings about missing implementation updates if the codebase likely expects partial changes across multiple files.
Drop speculative existence/arity audits of _ack_skill_path — monkeypatch.setattr already raises AttributeError on rename, a point the reviewers themselves concede.
Dismiss logic findings concerning trivial discrepancies between code comments and test assertions, such as off-by-one counts for line breaks.
Dismiss feedback regarding brittle implementation checks in tests when behavioral verification is sufficient.
Do not flag technical implementation details in documentation history tables as redundant.
Dismiss suggestions to replace print statements with the logging module in fix commits.
Suppress speculative architectural critiques about hardcoded regex patterns or maintenance risks for newly implemented invariant gates.

Suppress multi-finding deep dives into scripts/push-guard.sh internals (temp-file perms, EXIT-trap rc preservation, URL encoding, hook distribution) when the script is absent from the diff, since unverifiable speculation about missing code gets dismissed.

Suppress PRA-TEST: the identical _SUBJECTIVE ∪ _MACHINE partition-strengthening suggestion for tests/test_gen_best_practices.py earned the top reward when typed PRA-REVIEW and the bottom reward when typed PRA-TEST.

Cut the flood of test-hygiene PRA-REVIEWs (prompt-substring coupling, byte-identity snapshots, negative-ordering assertions, injectable-signature warnings, truncated-diff 'confirm the implementation exists' requests) — humans dismiss a long list of hypothetical test-internal refactors and environment-artifact complaints far more than they act on them.
Critique the technical validity of the proposed logic (such as regex side effects on formatting) described in the changelog.

Don't speculate about hypothetical renderer heading special-casing — the
count is pinned by the fixture as written and the imagined desync is not a real regression signal.
Do not flag tests that verify internal implementation details or source code content as problematic.
Ignore suggestions to refactor test utilities or extract mocks into shared fixtures.
Identify when generic utilities are defined in domain-specific modules, causing unnecessary coupling.
Dismiss nitpicks regarding code style and readability in favor of functional correctness.
Do not file the duplication root-cause under PRA-MAINT — this repo's high-reward reviews consistently label it PRA-DRIFT, so use that higher-signal type.
Identify test brittleness arising from hardcoded HTML fragments or string splitting on volatile content.
Flag excessive narrative history and issue tracking numbers within inline comments or docstrings.
Dismiss minor style critiques regarding f-string concatenation or specific string formatting choices.
Avoid reporting on inconsistencies in whitespace or line break handling within HTML rendering logic.
Suppress feedback on test implementation details such as manual tag counting when functional testing is maintained.

Call out unneutralized </details> or raw HTML in the preserved body prematurely closing the fold, plus dedupe relying on the tail-position invariant — robustness findings that higher-reward reviewers acted on.
Verify API response structures to avoid silently skipping files when encountering unexpected data formats.
Prioritize explicit configuration checks over implicit string matching to prevent false positive platform detection.
Replace deprecated functions with portable, future-proof standard library alternatives.
Suppress warnings about platform compatibility heuristics that are covered by explicit configuration checks.
Don't litigate subjective visual-fidelity details like entity text displaying literally inside markdown code spans when the PR's own tests already pin the chosen neutralization behavior.
Insist on write-time enum/schema validation and a regression test at the tfgrpo ingestion path, since this cleanup only fixes the symptom and the pipeline will regenerate the 299 bad candidates.
Do not challenge the classification of deleted entries as hallucinations based on standard taxonomy values.

Skip DESIGN-labeled commentary on experience-store purges (rubric-conflation critiques, feedback-loop essays, version-bump semantics) — reviewers only reward the quarantine substance when it is filed as ROBUSTNESS or CORRECTNESS.
Verify that test files referencing new logic are accompanied by the corresponding implementation in the source code.
Identify and correct obvious factual errors in comments, such as invalid future dates.
Suggest replacing manual configuration steps described in workflow comments with automated logic to prevent operator error.
Avoid inferring strict operational requirements or race conditions from test docstrings without confirming the implementation details.
Do not speculate about internal implementation requirements, such as sorting cache keys, based solely on test assertions.
Refrain from drawing conclusions about architectural limitations or user impact for custom functions based exclusively on unit test mock setups.
Do not use PRA-TEST-ROBUSTNESS; brittle-assertion findings belong under PRA-TEST-FRAGILE, the label reviewers respect.
Always verify that the diff is complete before flagging syntax errors or claiming implementation gaps.
Do not flag syntax errors that appear to be caused by truncated or incomplete diff boundaries.
Suppress changelog formatting suggestions about embedded slogans and bold emphasis — humans ignore non-blocking style advice on a one-line message correction.
Prioritize findings that critique the statistical validity, decision thresholds, and maintenance automation of configuration updates.
Ignore findings flagging future-dated comments in snapshot files as these are likely intentional simulation placeholders.
Dismiss findings recommending the removal of hardcoded statistics from explanatory comments unless they cause parsing errors.
Do not demand a summary digest repeat the full command details that SKILL.md already carries as the executable source.
Flag any discrepancy where the changelog lists new files or features that are completely absent from the provided diff.
Immediately block the review if security-critical scripts mentioned in the changelog are missing from the diff.
Do not raise issues regarding trivial metadata errors like future release dates when the diff lacks implementation code.

Avoid speculative doc findings on version-bump PRs (confirm PR #214 is merged, sweep hypothetical pinning docs for stale version references) unless you can cite an actual stale file — unverifiable 'confirm/sweep' doc asks get ignored on release commits.
Suppress resource leak warnings for short-lived read-only file operations in test utility functions.
Flag critical inconsistencies between the PR description and the diff when claimed code changes are missing.
Do not review specific workflow implementation details if the workflow files are absent from the diff.
Avoid generating configuration audit findings based solely on changelog text when the configuration files are missing.
Ensure that unexpected scanner exit codes trigger a hard failure rather than a neutral status to enforce a fail-closed security policy.
Warn that removing path exclusions for dependency directories will likely generate false positives that block valid development work.
Avoid suggesting automated updates for pinned security tool versions where stability and reproducibility are prioritized.
Skip raising hypothetical concerns about future JSON schema changes unless the current parsing logic is demonstrably fragile.
Do not request documentation enhancements or explanatory comments as critical findings during urgent workflow fixes.
Ensure that changes to detection logic are reflected in all related documentation and configuration hints to maintain cross-rule consistency.
Do not request additional test cases for minor edge patterns if the core logic implementation is correct.
Dismiss security warnings about `pull_request_target` usage for strictly read-only scanning jobs.
Suppress configuration findings questioning IP allowlists for private network ranges.

Suppress PRA-TEST requests for loader/schema validation of inert YAML seed files unless the reviewer demonstrates the file is actually wired into the prompt injector, as the lone such demand here rode in the -1-dismissed review.
Do not raise issues regarding missing source code diffs or refuse to review based solely on limited documentation changes.

Do not relitigate the PR's core mechanism (empty commit as trigger) with speculative redundancy arguments, especially when the CHANGELOG already states the rationale — reviewers reject design second-guessing on doc-only changes.
Do not flag information density in status lines or potential mobile formatting issues as review concerns.
Do not flag signature changes in internal orchestrator components as breaking changes requiring version bumps or coordination.
Avoid criticizing hardcoded indentation values in template rendering logic as robustness issues.
Do not request audits of truncation logic to detect markdown structure boundaries or mid-string corruption.
Do not require explicit verification of call sites for internal refactors unless a specific bug is identified.
Do not flag inconsistencies between PR descriptions and diffs if the context provided is limited to documentation.
Verify that all referenced local files exist and links resolve correctly to prevent user-facing 404 errors.
Identify and flag obvious factual errors such as incorrect dates or contradictory information.
Suppress 'grep the codebase for consumers' and silent-reset warnings on data shrinks — authors dismiss consumer-impact speculation that cites no actual broken lookup.
Do not report missing implementation for release PRs that only contain changelog and version updates.
Avoid flagging hypothetical security or formatting risks based on variable interpolation or test names without concrete evidence of the defect in the code.
Verify that unit tests cover new logic such as signal adoption and seed parsing mechanisms.
Ignore minor skips in sequential version numbers unless they violate strict release management policies.
Prioritize identifying logic that allows PR changes to self-suppress security findings during the review process by reading from the working tree.
Do not report the use of `importlib.reload` in test fixtures as a reliability or race condition concern.
Dismiss warnings about shadowing built-ins when importing internal framework modules like `touchstone.re`.
Ensure that environment variables introduced in workflow files are synchronized with the corresponding constants in the codebase.
Remove redundant conditional checks in helper functions that are already guaranteed by the caller's logic.
Dismiss potential security risks from standard string splitting operations unless unsafe library calls are involved.
Do not flag log messages containing non-English characters as encoding issues if the repository context supports them.
Avoid flagging increased resource usage as a performance issue when the change intentionally expands the processing window.

Lead every stale-value fix with the root cause — import the fallback constant from pr_agent_runner.py instead of swapping one hardcoded literal (32768) for another (128000) that will silently drift again.
Verify that files the code comments claim derive from __version__ (e.g. the SECURITY.md support window) actually reflect the new release instead of trusting the 注释.

Run a repo-wide grep for the stale value '32768' — especially SECURITY.md and CHANGELOG.md, which the warning message itself cross-references — and fix all live occurrences in this same PR, leaving historical changelog entries untouched.
Question observable design choices such as regression tests coupled wholesale to private underscore helpers and dedupe lacking sanity arbitration, which top-tier reviewers engaged with substantively.

Avoid generic 'verify the claim at HEAD' bug-verify notes; fold any needed checks into PRA-VERIFY with concrete semantic depth (unset vs empty handling, provider-dependent defaults, exact quote matching).
Never spend a finding on no-action changelog confirmations ('structure matches, no action needed') — reviewers reward findings requiring work, not approvals.
Frame findings as cheap, checkable consistency questions on the changed files — SECURITY.md supported range, hardcoded 0.2.7 literals in tests/scripts, changelog date vs actual tag date.
Deduplicate the two overlapping tests with clear split responsibilities (pointer presence vs layout) and rename `test_ack_section_readable_layout` to match its new link-only content.
Credit the clean release-prep structure and the explicit 'zero behavior change' parity note, since reviewers on this repo reward that transparency in release PRs.

Don't demand idempotency guards or extra test matrices for intentional double-escaping of pre-existing entities—one docstring line in `_html_text` noting the behavior is the actionable fix, as the higher-reward review did.
Do not demand proof of the 'zero behavior change' claim via env-semantics edge cases (empty-string vs missing variable) — reviewers dismiss verification requests about code absent from the diff.
Omit post-merge release mechanics advice about tag naming and publish-workflow triggers — it lives outside the diff and gets dismissed.
Avoid dumping merge-time chore lists (tag the commit, build smoke test, recheck SECURITY.md) — they duplicate question-framed checks and read as noise.

Stop relitigating patch-vs-minor bumps for additive artifact fields or demanding full field schemas on release PRs — maintainers dismiss versioning pedantry when the changelog already discloses the addition.
Drop wording audits of '契约零变化'-style claims that hinge on zero-change vs no-breaking-change distinctions; humans treat these as semantic quibbles on a release-only diff and ignore them.
For metadata-only release PRs, demand confirmation of the mechanical release checklist: v0.3.7 tag creation, pyproject dynamic-version read via CLI --version, and pipeline trigger.
Flag hardcoded release dates and heading-format drift against prior entries, but fold these into PRA-RELEASE-CONSISTENCY rather than splitting them into a separate type.
Don't request repo-wide dangling-reference sweeps for a deletion PR whose own tests already assert the removed content is absent.
Never flag possibly-unused imports as 'if' speculation on a pure-deletion PR—verify consumers with grep first or stay silent.
Do not demand widening sync tests to enumerate every individually pinned phrase — coverage-expansion wishlists that merely add more string assertions read as noise and get ignored.

Demand the actual deletion predicate and canonical finding_type allowlist behind the 'hallucinated' label, and require the 11 surviving entries to be diffed byte-identical against their pre-PR versions.

Stop requesting cleanup scripts, manifests, summary tables, or enumerations of surviving entries on data purges — both penalized reviews show authors dismiss reproducibility paperwork on one-off chore PRs.
Do not propose CI schema validation, parse checks, or loader smoke tests for data-only changes — authors dismiss speculative validation infrastructure on chores with no code under test.
Skip demands to fix the ingestion pipeline or add canary/rollback plans on a one-off data cleanse — authors treat root-cause prevention as out of scope for a chore and penalize it.

Do not demand repopulation plans or before/after review-quality comparisons when a data store shrinks — this repo has long-learned suppression of PRA-COVERAGE and both negative-reward reviews confirm it is dismissed again here.

Suppress PRA-REVIEW findings that meta-critique calibration config like .touchstone/seeds.yaml — statistical-significance quibbles, feedback-loop and staleness speculation, comment-vs-structured-metadata demands, and unverifiable-snapshot complaints — since the only review carrying nine of them scored -1 while clean reviews scored 0.0, showing humans dismiss process speculation that is not a concrete defect.

On release PRs whose diff is only CHANGELOG plus the version bump, raise the changelog-vs-diff artifact reconciliation once as a concrete verification action (confirm each advertised file actually landed via its linked PR before tagging).
When hand-maintained README metrics have already drifted once, recommend the specific mechanical fix (CI-injected cloc/coverage numbers between markers) rather than merely noting the drift.
Do not escalate the already-stated missing-artifact observation into BLOCKER/RELEASE severity or restate it under new finding types; one grounded confirmation request carries full weight.

When a release PR will be blocked by its own not-yet-active fail-closed gate, flag the chicken-and-egg immediately and force an explicit, documented merge path (admin override or recorded exemption) before tagging.
For version-bump release PRs whose diff is only CHANGELOG plus __version__, verify that every PR number cited in the release notes is actually merged to the release branch before approving.

Require in-repo evidence (regression tests actually running in CI, or the merged security PR) for any security-guarantee claim in release notes, because a changelog can assert protections that do not exist on the branch.
On every release bump, grep the repo for stale hardcoded version strings (SECURITY.md supported range, docs, lock files, CI badges) so only the dynamic source of __version__ needs editing.
Do not relitigate which existing changelog section falls under the new version heading; reviewers treat heading-placement pedantry on release PRs as noise.
Do not flag a missing Keep-a-Changelog compare linkref unless the repo demonstrably defines one for every prior version; it is cosmetic and dismissed.
Do not comment on the changelog date's format, timezone, or tag-day alignment; date-style nitpicks are ignored on version-bump PRs.

Challenge version-scheme policy head-on: when a PR ships features under a patch bump (0.3.6→0.3.7), demand either a minor bump (0.4.0) or a documented deliberate exception — this was the only finding unique to the highest-reward review.

Cross-check the changelog's PR summary against its actual subsections and demand the missing user-facing entry when a cited PR (#218 preflight 文案对齐) has no section, plus verification of the 'N 个 PR' count against git history.
Insist that internal review-process narration (评审 3 轮收敛、边界收口) be stripped from user-facing CHANGELOGs and that release headings annotate all shipped changes, not just one.

On every release PR, sweep the whole repo for stale hardcoded old versions (SECURITY.md, README, tests) that would break the __version__ single-source-of-truth claim, and bundle the compare-link, release-date, and tag checks into this one finding.

Drop this type — it relabels the PRA-DOCS missing-entry finding, and repeating the same point under a bespoke CHANGELOG-* label reads as noise; only the top-two reviews that used PRA-DOCS got traction.
Drop this type — the hardcoded-version sweep belongs under PRA-RELEASE-CONSISTENCY, and restating it under a new label adds nothing.
Drop this type — the hardcoded-date check is already covered by PRA-CONSISTENCY/PRA-RELEASE-CONSISTENCY in higher-reward reviews.
Drop hedged keep-a-changelog link nits (若不使用该惯例可忽略) — self-excusing conditional findings get dismissed; raise only under PRA-RELEASE-CONSISTENCY if the convention is confirmed in the file.
Drop this type — it restates the PRA-STYLE process-narration point, which was already acted on when framed as PRA-STYLE.
Drop this type — a third relabeling of the same process-narration point; one PRA-STYLE finding per review suffices.
Suppress minor naming-drift nits (列表页可见性 vs PR 列表页零点击可见性) as standalone findings — mention wording alignment only inside an existing PRA-STYLE note.
Drop speculative diff-context questions (whether 未发布 content was intentionally scoped to 0.3.7) that the reviewer can resolve with a single file read.
Drop bundled metadata checklists that recombine date+link+count checks already raised individually — such aggregation appeared only in the two lowest-reward reviews.
Drop unverifiable 'confirm the PRs are actually in the baseline' demands with no evidence a change is missing — speculation about release integrity reads as filler.
Drop speculative inferences that a phrase (未知决策态不谎报) implies a hidden behavior change — flag behavior-accuracy issues only with evidence the behavior actually changed.

File PRA-MAJOR when a docs trim removes deploy-flow safeguards—touchstone doctor (exit 0 = go-live self-check) and the TOUCHSTONE_OUTPUT_DIR rule that stops concurrent PR reviews overwriting touchstone-metrics.json.
Lead with PRA-ACCURACY when new positioning copy like 'AI Committer' contradicts the repo's documented advisory-only model where deterministic gates, not AI, decide merges.

Use PRA-DOC-COVERAGE to demand a destination check: confirm docs/DEPLOYMENT.md actually covers doctor, dry-run, .touchstone/ policy files, and the Secrets→Variables migration before accepting a section deletion as pure simplification.
Run a PRA-LINK-ROT grep across README, docs/, skills/, and workflow comments for dead references to the deleted 本地命令/规模与状态 anchors before merge.
Reserve PRA-MINOR for cheap one-line restorations, e.g. a 更多文档 pointer to .touchstone/ config or the offline pip install -e contributor entry.
Raise user-directed copy changes as PRA-QUESTION ('confirm the Committer wording and AI-generated-code tagline narrowing are intentional?') so the author answers intent instead of defending prose.
Keep PRA-NIT for drop-in fixes such as stripping the '（用户指示）' process attribution from CHANGELOG entries.
Use PRA-STYLE sparingly to push CHANGELOG toward describing user-visible change instead of re-quoting README marketing copy.
Stop minting PRA-DOCS-INFO-LOSS / PRA-DOC-INFO-LOSS / PRA-DOC-OPS-LOSS variants; restate deleted-content findings under canonical PRA-DOC-COVERAGE or PRA-MAJOR.
Do not file PRA-NAMING-AMBIGUITY or PRA-DOC-NAMING; the Committer-vs-advisory tension is already owned by PRA-ACCURACY.
Drop PRA-DOCS-DEADLINK and PRA-LINK-RISK duplicates; anchor checks belong under PRA-LINK-ROT.
Skip PRA-CHANGELOG-STYLE; humans dismiss bespoke type names for the same changelog nit already covered by PRA-STYLE/PRA-NIT.
Don't file PRA-DOC-COMPAT for the Secrets→Variables migration note; fold it into the existing PRA-DOC-COVERAGE destination-check finding.
Suppress PRA-DOCS-CONSISTENCY remarks about changelog bullets referencing deleted scale numbers; readers treat them as bookkeeping noise.
Suppress PRA-DOC-ACCURACY marginal qualifiers like the verify 'reference-level' maturity note unless the omission changes user behavior.

Emphasize a whole-repo grep for stale copies of changed 同源 constants (leftover '每 2 分钟' in other skill files, docs pages, templates, or tests asserting the old verbatim string) because this repo's drift tests only pin the phrases touched in the diff, so stale copies elsewhere survive CI.

Emphasize that any clarification of an existing rule (the §4 reinterpretation of §6-2's '落进测试套件') must be written at the canonical section itself or carry an explicit cross-reference, per the repo's three-place-sync 同源 discipline.

Emphasize extending test_skill_doc_sync (or a grep-style test) to pin README's copy of the cadence phrase '每 1 分钟检查一次', since README is the fourth hand-edited copy and this PR itself is proof that manual lockstep edits drift.

Emphasize that relaxed magic caps like len(frag) < 700 must print the actual digest length in the assertion message or derive the bound from line count, so the next bump is data-driven and unbounded digest growth stays visible.

Emphasize the operational cost of doubling the poll rate (≈60 checks/hour per PR) with one concrete line telling agents to do a single cheap check per tick via a scheduled task so multi-round sessions don't trip secondary rate limits.

Suppress re-typed duplicates of the stale-string grep (PRA-CROSS-FILE-CONSISTENCY, PRA-REPOWIDE-CONSISTENCY) — the check belongs under one PRA-DOC-DRIFT finding and extra types just dilute the review.
Suppress INTERNAL-CONSISTENCY and CROSSREF-VERIFY rewrites of the §6-2 placement issue — they restate the PRA-SINGLE-SOURCE finding reviewers already act on.
Suppress COVERAGE-GAP and DRIFT-GAP re-files of the README sync-test suggestion — it is the same PRA-TEST-COVERAGE point already emphasized.
Suppress BRITTLE-ASSERTION and TEST-MAINTAINABILITY variants of the frag-cap critique — the actionable core (print the margin or compute the bound) is already covered by PRA-TEST-GUARD.

Suppress speculative what-if readings of the doc (findings arriving after the ② full run, 'findings 清零' vs waived/split 收敛, cadence-stacking misreads in DOC-CLARITY style) — these hypotheticals padded the lowest-reward reviews and humans dismissed them.

Suppress cosmetic nits (CHANGELOG '### 变更' subsection shape, off-by-one comment enumeration in tests, digest wording drift like '最新评审评论' vs '最新一条 bot 评论') — nit density correlates with reward dropping from -3.0 to -4.0.
Suppress title-vs-diff wording quibbles (PR says 'README 精简' but nothing was slimmed) unless they block merge — this surfaced only in the lowest-reward review and humans let it pass.
Import the runner's DEFAULT_CONTEXT_TOKENS constant and interpolate it into the preflight warning instead of hardcoding a new 128000 literal that will drift again.
Verify at current HEAD that pr_agent_runner.py's fallback is actually the constant 128000 (and unconditional) before asserting it in user-facing text.
Grep tests for the stale 32768 assertion and add a regression test asserting the warning text equals the value imported from the runner constant.
Run a repo-wide grep for 32768 in SECURITY.md, README, and docs since the warning itself directs readers there and fixing only preflight.py half-fixes the drift.
Do not push further rewording of the warning's 过小/过大 framing — the lowest-reward review shows extended copy-editing of an already-corrected string is discounted.

Lead with the two concrete CHANGELOG defects a release reviewer fixes on sight: the missing [0.3.6] compare-link reference (plus the re-based [未发布] link) and the hard-coded release date that must equal the actual v0.3.6 tag date.
After the dynamic __version__ bump, direct reviewers to grep for stale '0.3.5' literals (SECURITY.md supported range, docs, CI pins, release scripts) since any missed copy silently drifts.
Verify PR #216 is actually merged before this release PR lands and remind them to push tag v0.3.6, so the changelog never documents a change that isn't shipped.
Skip nits about the parenthetical release heading or anchor-slug churn — humans dismiss cosmetic Keep-a-Changelog formatting advice.
Do not coach on the PR title implying the Secrets→Variables migration lives in this diff — humans dismiss title-wording suggestions on pure release-bookkeeping PRs.
Omit generic post-merge checklists (create tag, draft GitHub Release notes, confirm publish workflow) — humans dismiss boilerplate process steps not tied to anything in this diff.
Run the contract/sync tests and confirm CLI --version reports the new version before endorsing a release that asserts zero behavior change.
When a version number is skipped, keep the single transparent note (optionally a deterministic stub heading) so tooling and users treat the gap explicitly.
Do not spend notes validating that a patch-level bump is semantically correct — it restates the author's own claim and triggers no action.
Do not re-litigate the 'zero contract change' assertion in a separate finding; fold it into the single test-verification request.
Skip speculative quibbles about PR-title metaphors ('空提交') that don't affect the diff or the shipped artifacts.
Do not demand justification for an already-documented version skip or suggest reverting to the skipped number — second-guessing an explicit recorded decision gets ignored.
Don't split the SECURITY.md support-range check into its own finding; it is one item inside the single stale-version grep.
Suppress single-source-of-truth restatements that only re-describe the pyproject dynamic-version mechanism without a new actionable check.
Avoid a separate stale-reference sweep finding when PRA-CONSISTENCY already covers the same repository-wide check.
Don't create a separate link-reference finding; the compare-range check belongs inside PRA-RELEASE-CONSISTENCY.

When a sequence or wording string changes in multiple doc files, grep the entire repo for the old phrasing (README, docs/, other skills, golden/snapshot outputs) and run the full suite, not just the touched test.
Skip semantic quibbles about individual words like "必" or "同点承载" that do not change the executable steps agents follow.
Drop the nitpick asking to unify the two phrasings of issue #211 in the changelog — reviewers consistently dismiss terminology-consistency suggestions on release notes.

Do not demand audit-level verification of cited numbers (e.g., that #212 really contains '11 regression tests') that a metadata-only diff cannot check — such unactionable verification requests get ignored.

Confirm that changelog-described behavior actually exists on the release tree (lockfile at 0.44.0, new output fields emitted) and that git log v0.3.1..HEAD contains no unrecorded changes, otherwise the release ships fiction.

Keep at most this one finding on docs-only PRs: demand the exact commands behind hand-copied scale numbers (the 818→1220 drift proves staleness) and push for script/CI generation, because it is the only claim humans can objectively verify.
Raise the docs-describe-code-not-in-diff concern exactly once as a merge-order confirmation question, never as a blocking defect, since the companion implementation usually already sits on main.
Do not demand the README collapse to a link when it already declares SKILL.md authoritative — humans accept summary-plus-source and dismiss single-source purism.
Do not demand the README spell out tie-breaks, timezone frames, or bot-identity detection — humans treat SKILL.md as the contract's home and dismiss README-level spec-lawyering.
Do not flag the created_at reference frame as ambiguous — humans dismiss timezone and clock-skew lectures on a summary paragraph that defers to the skill spec.
Skip hypothetical nested-marker scanning semantics — humans dismiss invented edge cases with no observed failure and no code in the diff.
Do not ask the README to restate that the bot folds only its own comments — humans consider that self-evident from the system's role.
Do not demand softening absolute phrasing like 'always read the latest' — humans dismiss wording-hedging requests that propose property tests outside the diff.
Do not audit README stop-condition enumeration against SKILL.md completeness — humans accept the explicit deferral to the skill and dismiss cross-doc reconciliation demands.
Do not relitigate the layered-defense framing by arguing L3 is not a runtime backstop — humans dismiss philosophy-of-defense quibbles on marketing prose.
Do not propose new audit features like comment-visible neutralization counts or step-failure escalation from a docs review — humans treat it as scope creep beyond the diff.
Do not demand a marker-registry pointer or maintenance note in the README — humans dismiss registry bookkeeping suggestions on summary tables.
Do not inject GitHub secondary-rate-limit and ETag/incremental-fetch ops advice into a README review — humans dismiss ops-playbook scope creep entirely.
Do not debate escaped-versus-rendered fold readability tradeoffs — humans dismiss subjective readability notes that suggest redesigning intentional safety choices.

Do not flag the touchstone-ack 2-minute polling loop as unbounded on terminal PRs—humans dismissed even this concrete safety framing, treating the documented convergence/escalation stop rules as sufficient.
